target_customer: B2B merchants and marketplaces whose business buyers want net terms, later lenders needing SMB credit infrastructure
problem: Small businesses buying from suppliers, especially across borders in Latin America, lack trade credit and slow payments hurt sellers.
business_model: Take rate on financed B2B purchases (about 26 percent of a marketplace's gross merchandise value in 2022 per TechCrunch), later credit infrastructure licensing
product_category: B2B buy now pay later and credit infrastructure

founders.name: Lawrence Lin Murata
founders.background_notes: YC page: led AI platforms and data science at Nauto; co-founded CS+Social Good at Stanford.

founders.name: Alice Deng
founders.background_notes: YC page: product manager at Dropbox. The two met at a hackathon in 2016 per a Yahoo profile.

investors: angel founders from Dropbox, DoorDash, Opendoor, Plaid, PlanGrid, Mercury and Pilot

technical_complexity.rationale: Payments, underwriting and fraud models for thin file businesses; standard fintech engineering plus nontrivial risk modeling.

defensibility.rationale: Transaction and repayment data improve underwriting over time and the company later built a cash flow score, but rivals could build similar BNPL products.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source names incumbents that copied it; the company later partnered with J.P. Morgan, IKEA and Amazon according to dated news.

market_need_then: TechCrunch in Nov 2021 reported 15 times growth in gross merchandise volume in 30 days; by April 2022 it financed over 2,500 businesses in the US and Mexico. These are company reported figures.

branding.name_origin: CEO says an investor advised hiring for slope (growth rate) over y-intercept (past experience), inspired by a 2016 Sam Altman tweet.

identity.voice_and_tone: Positioned as Stripe for global B2B payments

branding.brand_signature: Hire for slope name story tied to Sam Altman
branding.community_and_virality: Press attention tied to Sam Altman backing; no merch or community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name has a quotable origin and investor press, but the sources show no independent brand awareness or community.

pivots.from: Cross border B2B buy now pay later for Latin American commerce
pivots.to: Credit infrastructure for business lending (embedded capital, cash flow score, AI transaction model)
pivots.why: The current site describes credit infrastructure; the shift date and reason were not found.

outcome_analysis: Slope raised an 8 million dollar seed in November 2021, a 24 million Series A in April 2022, 30 million in 2023 and a 65 million equity and debt package in July 2024 led by J.P. Morgan. Company reported growth and enterprise partners such as IKEA and Amazon suggest real traction, and the offering moved toward credit infrastructure. No exit, layoffs or shutdown were found.
notes: Competitors: the Nov 2021 and Apr 2022 TechCrunch pieces name no rivals; a geo.sig.ai profile lists Resolve but is undated, so the list is empty. The 2023 and 2024 rounds are labeled other because sources do not state a stage; the 2024 round mixes equity and debt (press says 77M equity and 175M debt total, 252M overall). The 2023 round's investors are from a Medium title and TechCrunch headline (USV and Sam Altman). Founding year was not stated on opened pages. Dealroom totals conflict and were ignored.
